checkpoint: F: falling blocks are vanilla FallingBlockEntity, not a one-cell-per-tick block move
goal: Match vanilla's position, acceleration, landing and save for falling blocks instead of keeping the block in the world and moving it one cell a tick.

contract.gravity: getDefaultGravity() = 0.04; applyGravity adds -gravity to dy each tick
contract.drag: none (the post-move Entity.bP is portal handling)
contract.landing: when the feet reach the top face of the first solid block below; the block is placed there and the entity discarded

changes.model: Fall { eid, x, y, z, dy, state, time }; the block leaves the world on spawn_fall
changes.physics: falling_tick integrates dy -= 0.04 and lands on the support top
changes.wire: interest_tick spawns type 40 with object data = state; falling_tick broadcasts 0x70 position and 0x42 destroy
changes.save: FAL2 records id/position/velocity/state/age; FAL1 (legacy cells) converts on load and removes the block
changes.cold: an entity in a cold chunk is kept, not ticked

mutations: tools/mutation_check.sh pairs each gate with a change: self/above-cell check removed, a passing entity suppressing a new block, asset set -> hand list of 3, gravity 0.04 -> 0.08, landing cell +1, cold-chunk check removed, FAL2 tag changed; fast-fall sweep start old->new; FAL1 explicit air -> non-air; falling-tick clone -> mem::take; UPD_DEFER push -> discard; place_block notifies requested state -> ghost update
limits: note_falling skips py <= MIN_Y, so a gravity block at the world floor is not converted.
canSurvive correction, levelEvent(2001) and cancelDrop are not implemented; the 19 falling states are neither EntityBlock nor hurting blocks, so BlockEntity/setHurtsEntities/causeFallDamage are N/A.
The entity is a point: no bounding box.

oracle.input: stone floor at y=150, sand placed at y=153, chunk kept ticking by a connected CLI client
oracle.vanilla: sand lands at y=151 (only 150 and 151 non-air, no falling_block entity left)
oracle.mc_spine: sand lands at y=151 (final_column {150: stone, 151: sand})
oracle.result: same landing cell on both servers for the same input
oracle.note: The oracle observes the landing cell; the tick-by-tick position is pinned by the unit test against the bytecode formula.

integration_review_fixes: The support scan sweeps from the old feet to the new feet, so a one-block platform crossed in a sub-block step is a landing, not a tunnel. (Codex integration review P2)
A migrated legacy FAL1 cell records explicit air instead of removing its overlay entry, so a non-air generated base is not exposed under the new entity. (Codex integration review P2)
falling_tick snapshots the queue instead of draining it, so a SIGTERM/save-all save during the pass sees every in-flight entity (Codex integration review P1).
block_updated queues a neighbour update past the recursion cap and drains it iteratively, so a gravity column taller than 64 still converts (Codex integration review P2).
spawn_fall and falling_tick's landing placement run under a re-entrant SAVE_LOCK guard, so a signal-thread save cannot observe the block/entity transition midway (Codex integration review P2).
spawn_fall claims the block with set_block_if(..., Some(st)) so two threads cannot both create an entity for one block (Codex integration review P2).
place_block queues the post-conversion world state, so placing unsupported sand does not leave a ghost block update (Codex integration review P2).
